automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Leaf Update Watch

cutoff_window.rule: Only sources published or visibly updated within the last 7 days relative to run_timestamp qualify; ambiguous, missing, future, and boundary-only dates are excluded.

qualifying_updates.source_title: What’s New in New-Scale July 2026: AI Agents Need More Than Guardrails
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Exabeam announced July 2026 agent-security capabilities including open-source agent verification and telemetry projects, expanded AI observability with Claude support, additional Agent Behavior Analytics detections, and OWASP Agentic Top 10 coverage scoring.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Supports local guidance that user-visible and operator-visible telemetry should cover agent behavior, verification, and security posture rather than only application health.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Telemetry leaves should distinguish security and behavior signals from generic progress reporting when ingestion updates the wiki.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Route product and standard background upstream; keep only the local telemetry/governance implication in this wiki.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Monitoring Agentic AI in Production: 2026 Guide
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: MLflow describes agentic monitoring as tracking reasoning loops, tool calls, and state transitions across sessions, with both performance and quality metrics needed to detect semantic failures before users experience them.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Reinforces that local runtime telemetry should expose multi-step agent state and quality signals, not just infrastructure metrics.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Progress and telemetry pages should frame agent observability around traces, tool calls, state transitions, and quality checks.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Keep MLflow product details upstream-owned; ingest the local telemetry criteria only if updating the leaf.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Godot’s AI ban is a reality check for vibe coders
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Creative Bloq reports that Godot plans to ban AI-authored code, AI-submitted pull requests, and most AI-written human-to-human contribution text, citing low-quality PRs, reviewer burden, and inability of AI-heavy submitters to repair reviewed code.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Provides a concrete public example that generated-code review, PR packaging, and AI-assisted TDD guidance must account for maintainer burden and contributor responsibility.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Local practice should keep AI-generated changes small, reviewable, attributable, tested, and repairable by the submitting human or agent workflow.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Route Godot ecosystem policy background upstream; keep the local maintainer-burden lesson here.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Speed without control is a liability, not an advantage: GitLab study reveals AI code generation is outpacing controls
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TechRadar summarizes GitLab study findings that AI code generation increases speed, but review, validation, governance, provenance, and maintainability are becoming downstream constraints; 85 percent cited code review and validation as the bigger bottleneck.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Supports local coding-practice leaves that treat verification, provenance, and maintainability as first-class outputs of AI-assisted coding work.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Refactoring and PR packaging guidance should continue to emphasize traceable review evidence and maintainable diffs over raw generation speed.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Do not duplicate GitLab report background locally; ingest the local review/governance implication if needed.

qualifying_updates.source_title: AI coding agents can be tricked into installing malware via clean GitHub repositories
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Tom’s Hardware reports Mozilla 0din research showing a coding agent can be induced to run malware from a seemingly clean repository through indirect setup instructions, DNS TXT indirection, and helpful remediation behavior.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Local runtime harness guidance should treat cloned repositories, setup scripts, network access, and agent-helpfulness loops as execution risks in local model and coding-agent environments.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Local harness pages should prefer explicit execution gates, repository trust checks, and inspection of setup commands before agent-run commands execute.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Route vulnerability/ecosystem background upstream; retain local harness control implications.

qualifying_updates.visible_date_evidence: Changelog entry shows PR Reviews, July 2, 2026.
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: CodeRabbit published a PR review changelog entry for a quiet review profile, indicating continued product movement toward configurable AI review behavior.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Configurable review noise is relevant to intelligent-code-review guidance because AI review tools must balance useful findings with reviewer attention limits.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Review guidance should preserve the idea that review assistants need signal controls, not just broader coverage.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Use as product-specific evidence only if the leaf needs an example; upstream owns CodeRabbit product tracking.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Context Layer for AI Agents: Enterprise Guide 2026
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Atlan describes an agent context layer as governed business meaning between data systems and agents, covering semantic definitions, entity identity, policy enforcement, lineage, active metadata, and decision memory; it distinguishes context layers from RAG and semantic layers alone.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Supports context-router, knowledge-layer, rules-layer, thin-router, and analytics-context leaves by framing context as governed meaning and provenance rather than raw retrieval.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Context architecture guidance should keep retrieval separate from governed meaning, provenance, and decision memory.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Route vendor and standard background upstream; keep downstream lens on context-layer operating practice.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Context Engineering: The Complete 2026 Field Guide for AI Developers
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Taskade frames context engineering as managing system prompts, tools, memory, retrieval, and state, with patterns including persistent context restoration, tool gating, context compression, retrieval budgeting, and multi-agent context sharing.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Supports multiple context-architecture leaves by reinforcing durable distinctions between memory, retrieval, state, compaction, and routing.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Context leaves should continue to separate persisted state, curated memory, retrieval budget, and compaction responsibilities.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Keep Taskade product detail upstream-owned; ingest the context-architecture pattern implications only.
